title: Dantzig Proof Spine for Minimax (Ordered-Field Route)
body_html:
Dantzig Proof Spine for Minimax (Ordered-Field Route)

This proof-plan node records the alternative, ordered-field-generic route to the von Neumann minimax theorem. The primary route used by the library is the simplified Loomis induction over $\mathbb{R}$ (Minimax via the All-Ones Specialization of Loomis). The Dantzig route is retained because:

  1. It works over any linearly ordered field, not just $\mathbb{R}$ — a strict generalisation of Loomis.
  2. It yields a constructive simplex algorithm in Lean, useful as a future basis for executable extraction.
  3. Most of its algebraic scaffolding is already proved; only the simplex-termination step (the top-level dantzig_minimax induction) is open — tracked as the open issue Dantzig Simplex Termination (Open) in staged/.

Open. This route is not yet complete. The lone remaining gap is the simplex algorithm's finite-termination argument; see the proof-plan node linked above for the precise statement and intended approach.

Dantzig's proof represents the minimax theorem through an augmented linear system. A basis state stores rows of the inverse basis matrix, a lexicographic condition prevents cycling, and optimality inequalities encode the game-theoretic guarantees.

At an optimal basis, the extracted row strategy is nonnegative and satisfies the row player's guarantee inequalities. The same basis data extracts a column strategy for player II. The pivot step updates the inverse basis while preserving the lexicographic condition and strictly decreasing the leading row in lexicographic order.
proof_html:
The route starts from Dantzig's augmented system for the shifted positive payoff matrix. A basis state contains enough inverse-basis data to read off candidate row and column variables. If the current basis is not optimal, the pivot rule selects an entering and leaving variable so that feasibility is preserved and the lexicographic leading row strictly decreases. The lexicographic condition rules out cycles, so repeated pivots terminate. At the terminal basis, the optimality inequalities say exactly that the extracted row strategy guarantees the terminal value and the extracted column strategy caps the same value. Normalizing the extracted nonnegative variables gives mixed strategies, and undoing the initial constant shift gives the minimax equality for the original game.

References

  • [Dantzig, Sections 2-3] Dantzig, A Constructive Proof of the Min-Max Theorem, docs/dev/references/Dantzig, CONSTRUCTIVE PROOF OF THE MIN-MAX THEOREM.pdf. Constructive proof of the minimax theorem via simplex-style pivots.

lean_refs.name: fin_sum_succ
lean_refs.signature:
theorem fin_sum_succ {M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M] {n : ℕ} (f : Fin (n+1) → M) :
    ∑ k : Fin (n+1), f k = f 0 + ∑ k : Fin n, f k.succ
lean_refs.docstring: Sum over Fin(n+1) splits into f(0) + ∑ k : Fin n, f(k.succ).

lean_refs.name: optimal_basis_minimax
lean_refs.signature:
theorem optimal_basis_minimax (st : DantzigState m 𝕜)
    (A : Fin m → Fin n → 𝕜) (hopt : st.isOptimal A) :
    -- Player I conditions from (1)-(3):
    -- (1) xᵢ ≥ 0: from β₀·Uₖ ≤ 0, i.e. β₀,ₖ₊₁ ≤ 0, so xₖ = -β₀,ₖ₊₁ ≥ 0
    (∀ i : Fin m, 0 ≤ st.stratI i) ∧
    -- (3) x₀ ≤ ∑ aᵢⱼ xᵢ: from β₀·Pⱼ ≤ 0
    (∀ j : Fin n, st.value ≤ ∑ i : Fin m, st.stratI i * A i j) ∧
    -- Basis variables: basisVar j ≥ 0 (from lex condition on βⱼ₊₁)
    (∀ j : Fin m, 0 ≤ st.basisVar j)
lean_refs.docstring: An optimal basis gives valid mixed strategies and the minimax value.

lean_refs.docstring: Pivot update: β*ᵢ = βᵢ - (vᵢ/vᵣ)βᵣ for i ≠ r; β*ᵣ = (1/vᵣ)βᵣ.

lean_refs.name: dantzigPivot_lexCond
lean_refs.signature:
theorem dantzigPivot_lexCond
    (beta : Fin (m+1) → Fin (m+1) → 𝕜)
    (v : Fin (m+1) → 𝕜) (r : Fin (m+1))
    (hr : r ≠ 0) (hvr : v r > 0)
    (hlex : ∀ i, i ≠ 0 → LexPos (beta i))
    -- The lex-min rule (21): r achieves the lex-minimum of (1/vᵢ)βᵢ
    -- Lex-min rule (21): r achieves STRICT lex-minimum among all vᵢ > 0
    -- (strict because B⁻¹ rows are linearly independent)
    (hmin : ∀ i, i ≠ 0 → i ≠ r → v i > 0 →
      lexGt (fun k => beta i k / v i) (fun k => beta r k / v r)) :
    ∀ i, i ≠ 0 → LexPos (dantzigPivot beta v r (ne_of_gt hvr) i)

lean_refs.name: dantzigPivot_beta0_decrease
lean_refs.signature:
theorem dantzigPivot_beta0_decrease
    (beta : Fin (m+1) → Fin (m+1) → 𝕜)
    (v : Fin (m+1) → 𝕜) (r : Fin (m+1))
    (hr : r ≠ 0) (hvr : v r > 0) (hv0 : v 0 > 0)
    (hlex_r : LexPos (beta r)) :
    lexLt (dantzigPivot beta v r (ne_of_gt hvr) 0) (beta 0)

lean_refs.name: dantzig_minimax
lean_refs.signature:
theorem dantzig_minimax [Nonempty (Fin m)] [Nonempty (Fin n)]
    (A : Fin m → Fin n → 𝕜) :
    ∃ (x : stdSimplex 𝕜 (Fin m)) (y : stdSimplex 𝕜 (Fin n)) (v : 𝕜),
      (∀ j : Fin n, ∑ i : Fin m, x.val i * A i j ≥ v) ∧
      (∀ i : Fin m, ∑ j : Fin n, A i j * y.val j ≤ v)
